symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-05).
1184 of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills are AMI-channel reads that were received and exported before cutoff but rejected by billing import as high-consumption (E-12).
1785 of 3025 (59%) disputed bills involve ACTUAL, not estimated, reads (E-03), and the causal mechanism for this majority is not yet confirmed by evidence.
causal_chain: Rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, changes the billing-import high-consumption validation check to compare the raw AMI register value against 12-month m3 consumption history with no stated unit scaling (E-13).
Firmware v4.2 meters, rolled out 2026-06, report register values in units of 0.1 m3, a 10x difference from v3.x meters' m3 units (E-14).
Because BV-17 applies no unit scaling, legitimate high-consumption readings from v4.2 meters are miscompared against the m3-based history and misclassified as excessive.
Billing import rejects these valid, on-time AMI reads (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), accounting for 1184 of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read AMI-channel bills (E-12).

Rejected accounts fall back to estimate substitution, producing wrong (estimated) bills that affected customers dispute, contributing to the dispute-volume surge from ~600/month to ~1180-1260/month (E-05).

assumptions.statement: The firmware v4.2 tag on the 1184 rejected reads in E-12 is assumed to correspond to the same v4.2 meter population described in E-14's unit-mismatch finding, since no record directly joins individual meter IDs across both query results.

BV-17 is assumed to be the only operative validation rule affecting high-consumption classification during the Aug-Sep 2026 dispute window, with no undocumented patch beyond the two entries logged in E-13.
